question: How many other people must be in a room for an even chance that one of them shares your birthday?
move: A match with anyone comes quickly; a match with you comes slowly.
trap: Answering 23, the number for any two people sharing a birthday.
hint: Work out the chance that every one of them misses your date.
steps: Each person misses your birthday with probability 364/365.
You need (364/365) to the power n to fall to one half.
That needs n × (1/365) ≈ 0.693, the natural log of 2.
simply: Twenty-three people form 253 pairs, which is why any-pair matches arrive so soon.
reference: Feller, An Introduction to Probability Theory and Its Applications, vol. 1, 3rd edition, Wiley, 1968
